text:
alex: Heads up — right after the staged release at 10:03 UTC I'm seeing a sharp jump in 5xx from hosted inference in us-west. Error rate went from ~0.2% to ~7% over the last 5m. Users reporting timeouts and failed generations. Can SRE + runtime take a look? :rotating_light:

sre-oncall: On it. Are those 502s or 504s primarily? Any customer-facing errors we should prioritize?

alex: Mostly 502 and 503 gateway, a few 504s. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate and /v1/chat/stream. A few VIP customers emailed support.

deploy-bot: Deploy completed by maya at 2026-03-15T10:03:12Z. Rollout: staged-release v2 -> traffic 10%->90% (intended 10% canary).

maya: I pushed the staged-release config at 10:03. It flipped the router weight for the "staged-edge" rule to 90% by mistake (meant to be 10%). Rolling back now if that's the issue.

ryan: If staging traffic got 90%, that could overload older model variant pools. Seeing CPU/latency spikes on model-group-stable-1 and model-group-canary-odd.

sre-oncall: Checking logs and upstream error traces. Quick queries: `datadog query:request.status>=500 AND service:inference-edge AND env:prod AND region:us-west` -> big spike at 10:04.

sre-oncall: `kubectl get pods -l release=inference -n prod -o wide` shows many pods in model-group-canary-odd OOMKills and rapid restarts.

maya: Okay I'm initiating an emergency traffic-shift: set staged-edge weight back to 10% now. Command: `./routerctl set-weight staged-edge 10`

deploy-bot: Router weight change requested by maya at 2026-03-15T10:06:02Z. New staged-edge weight: 10%.

sre-oncall: Traffic shift in progress. Watching errors...

support: We have 3 severity-2 customer escalations in the queue, customers reporting intermittent 502s in us-west. They're asking for ETA. I told them we're investigating.

alex: Please prioritize customers on Dedicated plans. Put temporary fallback policy to route them to dedicated capacity if possible.

ryan: Trying to repro locally: long-context requests (>1024 tokens) to staged variant return 500 with stacktrace related to kv-cache lookup: `KeyError: prefix_cache_miss -> raise IndexError` — looks like a missing shim in the older canary runtime.

maya: That matches my suspicion. The canary build lacked the new prefix-cache compatibility layer; when traffic increased, cache misses surged and crashed the worker process under heavy concurrency. The bad rollout weight amplified it.

sre-oncall: Confirmed: upstreams returning 500 with body snippet: `runtime error: nil pointer deref in prefix_cache.go:142` and then proxy returns 502.

emily: I'm drafting a customer-facing message. Do we have an ETA for full recovery post-shift?

maya: If traffic stays on stable (we reverted to 10%), error rate should fall within 3-6 minutes as circuit breakers and restarts stabilize. I'll also cordon the problematic canary nodes to prevent new requests while we run a safer canary build.

deploy-bot: Node cordon requested by maya: `k8s cordon model-group-canary-odd` at 2026-03-15T10:09:10Z.

sre-oncall: Error rate dropping now from 7% -> 1.8% in last 2 minutes. Still watching.

support: Notifying the three escalated customers with an interim note: "we've reverted traffic to stable and are monitoring — we'll follow up with RCA" :white_check_mark:

ryan: Repro steps I used (for debugging):
1) `curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'X-Request-Mode: long' -d '{"prompt":"<~1500 tokens>","max_tokens":1024}`
2) Observe 500s on model-group-canary-odd pods; tail logs `kubectl logs <pod> -c runtime --since=10m` includes `prefix_cache.go` stack.

maya: Patch plan: build v2.1 with prefix-cache shim and a defensive nil-check, run a small 1% canary for 15m, then escalate to 10% if green. I'll coordinate with release engineering.

sre-oncall: For immediate mitigation we should also set the router fallback: route failing requests to dedicated backend for customers flagged as high priority. How do we opt-in customers quickly?

alex: Use the route-override table: `routectl set override --customer-id <id> --backend dedicated` — I can apply this for the three escalations.

emily: Applying messaging updates to status page: "Partial API errors in us-west for text generation endpoints; mitigation in progress; requesting customers will be routed to dedicated capacity where available." Draft pushed.

support: One of the customers (AcmeCorp) posted logs showing 502s starting at 10:04, matching spike. They've requested credit. I'll queue billing review after we confirm impact window.

sre-oncall: Monitor config: `datadog monitor:errors.inference-5xx-us-west`. Alert threshold temporarily lowered to catch regressions during rollout.

deploy-bot: Revert release requested by maya: `releasetool rollback staged-release v2 -> v1` at 2026-03-15T10:12:35Z.

maya: Rollback complete. Starting controlled redeploy of v2.1 to canary at 1% now. Command: `releasetool deploy staged-release v2.1 --canary 1%`

sre-oncall: Keeping an eye on OOMs and prefix-cache errors. If we see >1% 5xx in the next 10m we abort.

alex: Postmortem owners: maya (runtime), ryan (debugging), emily (communications). We need timeline, root cause (mis-weighted rollout + missing shim), customer impact table, and mitigation actions.

emily: Noted. I'll start the incident timeline doc and include the customer list.

support: All three escalated customers acknowledged our interim update and asked for an RCA within 24h.

ryan: For follow-up action items:
- Add circuit-breaker for prefix-cache failures to return 503 quickly rather than crashing pod.
- Add pre-deploy integration test that runs a long-context generation against canary runtime.
- Add router weight guardrail to prevent >25% unintentionally during staged releases.

maya: Agreed. I'll open the PRs and reference this thread.

sre-oncall: Error rate down to 0.4% now; system stable. Closing active mitigation. We'll still track post-deploy for 60m.

alex: Thanks everyone for the quick coordination. Please update the incident doc with timestamps and any logs you pulled. We'll schedule a 1h postmortem tomorrow. :coffee:

emily: I'll post the incident summary to #incidents once the doc is ready.

support: Closing customer comms loop after RCA.

maya: Follow-up: created PR #4527 for prefix-cache shim + defensive checks. Will request review after CI.

ryan: Created GH issue for router guardrail: infra/routers#180.

sre-oncall: Leaving notes in runbook: add step to verify staged-release weight before promote and to validate canary build compatibility.

alex: Good job. I'll mark this thread as part of the postmortem artifacts.
